notes.note: Neighbouring keys and almost the same tempo: start it early and take a long, unhurried blend.
Same key, so layer freely. Bring the new drums in under the melody and let the energy step up.
Two steps up the wheel: do not ride this one. Swap quickly at a phrase change for the lift.
Tempos match and the keys are neighbours. Blend for a full phrase, then trade the bass lines.
Same key, same tempo, same energy: the easiest mix of the night. Loop the outro and take your time.
Relative minor: the notes agree but the mood darkens. A slow blend lets the shift creep in.
One step round the wheel with a tiny tempo nudge. Mix on the percussion and swap bass at the phrase.
Same key, a little quicker. Ease the pitch up before you start so the blend itself stays clean.
Same key again and another small step up in tempo. Keep the blend short and let the drums carry it.
Matched in key, tempo and energy: this is the one to loop and layer for as long as you like.
Relative major, so the notes agree and the mood brightens. Time the swap for the high point of the set.
Neighbouring keys, same tempo. You are just past the peak, so take a longer blend and let it settle.
One step back round the wheel and slightly slower. Bring the pitch down gently while both tracks play.
Same key and a touch slower. Filter the highs out of the old track as the room starts to come down.
Neighbouring keys at matched tempo. A relaxed, even blend to close the set out.
